podcast.title: Estrangement from Tom DeLonge (2005-2022)
podcast.body: After Blink 182's indefinite hiatus began in 2005, Mark Hoppus and Tom DeLonge did not speak to each other for several years. "Tom DeLong and bass player Mark Hoppiz did not talk for years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Struggle with Depression and Anger (2018-2019)
podcast.body: During the period leading up to and during the recording of Blink 182's *Nine* album, Mark Hoppus struggled severely with depression. His wife encouraged him to pursue activities that brought him happiness, leading to the formation of Simple Creatures in 2018. His lyrics for *Nine* were notably darker, reflecting his internal battles, his anger over mass shootings (particularly one near Travis Barker's home), and his frustration with Donald Trump's policies. He was also not sober at this time. "But hold up though, Mark was struggling with depression during this time. And it was bad."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Justification for "Nine" Album Title (2019)
podcast.body: Mark Hoppus considered Blink 182's 2019 album *Nine* to be their ninth studio album, explaining that he counted *Buddha*, a 1994 album released before the band's name change from "Blink" to "Blink 182." He also stated, "Nine is the number of universal love." "Because Mark counted Buddha."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Accidental Public Cancer Revelation (2021)
podcast.body: On June 23, 2021, after three months of secrecy, Mark Hoppus accidentally posted a selfie from a chemotherapy infusion to his 1.2 million Instagram followers, instead of his private WhatsApp chat. The photo was captioned, "yes, hello, one cancer treatment, please." Though he deleted it immediately, the news spread, forcing him to issue a public statement confirming his diagnosis and treatment, which he later called "the best mistake I've ever made by far." "Instead, he posted it to Instagram and it went out to 1.2 million followers. It was captioned, yes, hello, one cancer treatment, please."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Grueling Chemotherapy Experience (2021)
podcast.body: Mark Hoppus underwent incredibly strong chemotherapy treatments. During one session, the drugs were so potent that his doctors advised his wife not to share a toilet with him for three days. He likened chemo to "being on the worst international overnight flight where you can't sleep or get comfortable," suffering from hair loss, constant pain, exhaustion, and persistent "brain fog" that made him feel "diminished mentally." "He says, chemo is like being on the worst international overnight flight where you can't sleep or get comfortable."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Large B Cell Lymphoma Diagnosis (2021)
podcast.body: In June 2021, Mark Hoppus discovered a concerning lump on his shoulder that was quickly diagnosed as stage 4 large B cell lymphoma, a fast-growing cancer type previously experienced by his mother. Terrified and believing he would die, he immediately began intensive chemotherapy. "It was something called large B cell lymphoma. This is a fast growing type of cancer, because the same cancer his mother had, and Mark's was stage 4."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Cancer-Free Declaration and Continued Screening (2022)
podcast.body: After undergoing intensive treatment through the end of 2021 and into 2022, Mark Hoppus was declared cancer-free. He was required to continue with screenings every six months. "Mark was declared cancer free, but had to continue screening every six months."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Healing of Friendships Through Cancer (2022)
podcast.body: His battle with cancer facilitated the repair of damaged relationships, particularly his friendship with Tom DeLonge, who offered immediate support. Mark reflected that this experience helped him appreciate his life, stating, "The cancer brought back friendships that I hadn't had in years. It healed my friendship with Tom."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Vocal and Physical Weakness Post-Chemo (2022)
podcast.body: During the recording of the *One More Time* album in January 2022, Mark Hoppus was not yet fully recovered from chemotherapy. The treatment had impacted his vocal cords, and his physical strength was still diminished, though he gradually regained it with each day of recording. "The chemo had done a number on his vocal cords and his strength still wasn't where it needed to be."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Fahrenheit 182 (2025) – Memoir
podcast.body: Mark Hoppus released a memoir titled *Fahrenheit 182* in April 2025, detailing his personal journey. "If you want to read more about Mark's journey, I highly recommend the memoir Fahrenheit 182, which came out in April 2025."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Adam's Song" Inspiration
podcast.body: He composed "Adam's Song" based on his experiences of loneliness while touring, particularly as a single individual among bandmates with girlfriends. The lyrical themes of depression and suicide were significantly influenced by a suicide letter he had encountered in a teen magazine. "Mark Hopper's remembered how lonely he got on tour."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: "Hi, My Name Is Mark" Clothing Line (Dates Unspecified)
podcast.body: Mark Hoppus developed his own clothing line, which he named "Hi, My Name Is Mark." "Meanwhile, Mark worked on his clothing line, which is called, hi, my name is Mark."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: B-cell Lymphoma Diagnosis and Announcement
podcast.body: Mark Hoppus was diagnosed with B-cell lymphoma Stage 4A, a type of blood cancer that his mother also experienced, in the spring of 2021 after noticing a peculiar knot in his shoulder. His diagnosis was accidentally made public on June 23, 2021, when an Instagram post meant for a select group of close friends was shared with everyone, featuring a picture of him in a chemo unit with the caption, "yes, hello, one cancer treatment, please." "That Instagram post was supposed to go out to a circle of close friends and no one else, but instead it went out to everyone."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Children's Hospital Charity Work (Dates Unspecified)
podcast.body: Mark Hoppus dedicated time to charity work, specifically for a children's hospital located in Los Angeles. "and he did charity work for a children's hospital in Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Construction Job
podcast.body: While Blink was in its formative years, Mark maintained a day job at a construction site, where he spent his days hauling bags of cement and sand. "Mark, for example, had a gig where he hauled bags of cement and sand at a construction site all day."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: DJ Sets and Emo Night (Dates Unspecified)
podcast.body: Spent several years performing occasional DJ sets at a club that regularly hosted an "Emo night." "He spent a couple of years playing occasional DJ sets at a club that held a regular Emo night."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Life and Family Trauma
podcast.body: Born in Washington, D.C., his family relocated to San Diego when his father, a Navy member, was transferred to a base there. This move coincided with his parents' divorce, a "broken family thing" that scarred him and led him to move around with his dad while his sister remained in San Diego with their mother. "Mark's father was in the Navy. He was born in Washington, DC, but ended up in San Diego when his father was transferred to the base there. That's when there was a divorce."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: Musical Discoveries
podcast.body: As a teenager, he found solace in music, discovering and becoming influenced by groups such as The Cure and The Smiths. He dedicated a significant portion of his earnings from working at Little Caesar's pizza to purchasing CDs. "He was scarred by the whole broken family thing, which explains why he discovered groups like the cure and the Smiths as a teenager."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: Previous Bands and Connection to Tom
podcast.body: Before joining Blink, Mark, who was a few years older than Tom DeLong and Scott Rainer, had already been a member of "a bunch of bands." He connected with Tom through his sister, who was dating one of Tom's friends, leading to their collaboration in songwriting. "Mark's sister was going out with one of Tom's friends, a connection was made and they started writing songs together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: Producing and Podcasting
podcast.body: During Blink-182's hiatus, Mark Hoppus took on producing projects for other artists. He also launched his own podcast titled "Hi, My Name is Mark," diversifying his activities beyond performing. "Mark Hopis took on a couple of producing projects and started a podcast called Hi, My Name is Mark."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

podcast.title: School Expulsion
podcast.body: During eighth grade, he was expelled from his school after showing up drunk to a basketball game. This expulsion serendipitously led him to register at another school for a semester, a key event that ultimately connected him with Tom DeLong. "One night he showed up at his school for a basketball game. He was in grade eight and he was drunk. That got him expelled, which meant he had to register at another school for one semester."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: Successful Treatment and Cancer-Free Status
podcast.body: Fortunately, Mark Hoppus's B-cell lymphoma was highly treatable. After undergoing a course of chemotherapy, he was declared cancer-free, mirroring his mother's eventual recovery from the same type of cancer. "The good news is that the cancer was very treatable and after undergoing chemo, Marc has been declared cancer-free, just like his mom eventually was."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: TV Appearances and "After School Radio" Podcast (Dates Unspecified)
podcast.body: Engaged in various TV projects and later launched his own podcast called "After School Radio." "He did some TV, and eventually got into podcasting with a show called, After School Radio, and he did charity work for a children's hospital in Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: TV Show Commitments
podcast.body: While working on the "Neighborhoods" album with Blink-182, Mark Hoppus had ongoing commitments to a TV show, which required him to frequently travel to New York. His busy schedule contributed to the difficulties and extended timeline in completing the album. "Mark Hopper said to keep flying to New York to work on a TV show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

podcast.title: Therapy Session Diagnosis Confirmation
podcast.body: The moment Mark Hoppus received confirmation of his cancer diagnosis was particularly dramatic; his cell phone rang with the doctor's news just as he was walking into an office to meet his therapist. This immediate call shaped the beginning of that therapy session, as he started it by stating, "Hi, yes, I just got a call and I found out I have cancer." "It was his doctor with the news. That's how the therapy session began."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Voice Strain during Dude Ranch
podcast.body: During the recording sessions for "Dude Ranch," Mark severely strained his voice by attempting to sing the album's first single, which was outside his vocal range. This injury accounts for his distinct vocal quality on the song "Dammit" and why Tom DeLong often sang the chorus when the band performed it live. "Mark had really screwed up his voice by trying to sing the first single from the song which was outside his range."

xref.title: Estrangement from Blink 182 (2005-2022)
xref.body: Following Blink 182's indefinite hiatus in 2005, Tom DeLonge and Mark Hoppus did not communicate for years. He notably quit Blink 182 twice, the second time in early 2015, either to focus on non-musical projects or due to an unwillingness to sign a contract requiring sole focus on the band. He remained estranged from Mark and Travis through 2021. "Tom DeLong and bass player Mark Hoppiz did not talk for years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation During Blink 182 Hiatus (Post-2005)
xref.body: This band was formed by Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker during Blink 182's indefinite hiatus, a period when Mark Hoppus and Tom DeLonge were not speaking. It was one of several solo/side projects that emerged during that time. "Bands like Tom's Angels and Airwaves and Mark and Travis's Plus 44."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Indefinite Hiatus (2005)
xref.body: An indefinite hiatus was announced on February 22nd, 2005, following a period of uncertainty and internal friction, during which Tom DeLonge and Mark Hoppus ceased communication for years. "Things got to the point where they couldn't continue, and an indefinite hiatus was announced on February 22nd, 2005."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Hospital Reunion (2008)
xref.body: Following Travis Barker's severe injuries from the plane crash, Mark Hoppus was among the first to visit him in the hospital, and Tom Delonge also made the trip. The three members of Blink-182 met in a "sobering reunion" at Travis's bedside, prompting a realization for all three about what truly mattered in their lives and relationships. "The three guys met up in the hospital in a pretty sobering reunion."

xref.title: Resurfacing Internal Issues (Late 2014)
xref.body: After their album *Dogs Eating Dogs* and more tours, the "old cracks returned" within the band. Issues between Tom DeLonge and Mark Hoppus, coupled with Travis Barker's fear of flying preventing overseas tours, came to a head in late 2014. "There were more tours, but the old cracks returned."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Matt Skiba's Recruitment and First Performance (2015)
xref.body: After Tom DeLonge's second departure, Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker decided against disbanding Blink 182 and recruited Matt Skiba from Alkaline Trio. Their first performance with Skiba on March 18, 2015, marked the first time Mark Hoppus played in Blink without Tom DeLonge, after which Skiba was made an official member. "Mark and Travis had no plans to kill Blink so they brought in Matt Skiba from Alkaline Trio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation for Depression (2018)
xref.body: This project was formed in 2018 by Mark Hoppus, in collaboration with Alex Gaskarth of All-Time Low, as an attempt to help Hoppus combat and break out of a period of severe depression. "Simple Creatures, Mark Hoppaz's side project born out of an attempt to break out of depression in 2018."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Not Sober During "Nine" Production (2019)
xref.body: During the period surrounding the creation of Blink 182's *Nine* album, Matt Skiba was not sober, paralleling a similar struggle experienced by Mark Hoppus at the time. "Same thing with Mads Keeba."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Reconciliation with Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker (2022)
xref.body: Upon learning of Mark Hoppus's cancer diagnosis, Tom DeLonge immediately reached out, leading to a crucial meeting in Mark's backyard that included Travis Barker. During this sit-down, they discussed life experiences, growth, and the realization that personal issues paled in comparison to Mark's health. This meeting was pivotal in healing damaged relationships and ultimately facilitated Tom's return to Blink 182. "When Tom's long heard about Mark, he was right there and soon there was a sit down in Mark's backyard."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tom DeLonge's Return and Reconciliation (2022)
xref.body: By mid-2022, rumors of a reunion circulated, leading to the band's social media accounts being wiped in October. On October 11, the official announcement was made that Tom DeLonge was back, and an album and a two-year world tour were planned. This reconciliation was spurred by Mark Hoppus's cancer diagnosis, which prompted Tom to reach out immediately. "And that's when news came down that Mark, Travis and Tom, came to the realization that it was time to bury all the animosities and get back to being Blink 182."

xref.title: Donna's Domain Review
xref.body: Mark Hoppus was described as a "hit with the ladies for obvious reasons" on Donna's Domain, a website that rates rock stars' penis size and sexual ability. This suggests a highly favorable assessment of his attractiveness or performance in the categories rated by the site. "Mark Hopis of Blink 182 is a hit with the ladies for obvious reasons."

xref.title: Formation and Origin of Name
xref.body: Plus 44 was formed by Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker during Blink-182's hiatus, initially conceived as a more electronic project. The band's name, "Plus 44," was inspired by the international dialing code for the United Kingdom, where the idea for the band first germinated among its members. "Mark Hoppiss and Travis Barker formed a band that they called Plus 44. That name comes from the code you have to use to call the UK."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Jerry Finn's Push for Other Projects
xref.body: Longtime producer Jerry Finn, along with Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker, made it clear they wanted to work on another project during Blink-182's hiatus. This desire led to the formation of Plus 44 by Mark and Travis, further solidifying the band's fragmentation. "It also didn't help the situation that the other two thirds of the band and their long time producer Jerry Finn made it very clear that they wanted to work together on another project."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Mark Hoppus's Isolation During Side Projects
xref.body: While Tom DeLonge and Travis Barker pursued side projects like Box Car Racer and The Transplants, Mark Hoppus "stayed on the sidelines quietly fuming," feeling betrayed that Tom had asked Travis to drum for Box Car Racer, a project that had an "old DIY vibe of early Blink." "Mark left the studio and wrote what he thought would be an instant rejection."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

xref.title: Mark Hoppus's Self-Reflection
xref.body: Bass player Mark Hoppus once expressed feeling that, despite being in his 20s, he was "still acting like a dumb teenager," reflecting the juvenile and goofy attitude often associated with pop punk. He reportedly "felt bad about that." "Base player Mark Hopper realized that he was in his 20s, but he was still acting like a dumb teenager. He felt bad about that."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Plus 44 Tour Experience
xref.body: The tour supporting the album "When Your Heart Stop's Beating" was a highlight for Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker (members of Plus 44), providing them the opportunity to play small clubs again after a long time, which was a re-energizing experience. During this tour, Travis Barker broke his arm during a video shoot, causing him immense pain and forcing him to miss several gigs. "The best part about it was the tour where Mark and Tom got to play small clubs for the first time in a long time. That was really energizing."

xref.title: Tom Delonge's Desire for Break
xref.body: Tom Delonge's decision to take a break stemmed from feeling the intense grind of the band's schedule and needing at least six months to decompress. He was disappointed that Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker didn't fully understand his need for this extended time away. "The story seems to be that Tom just wanted a break from the grind and he was disappointed that the other two guys didn't understand why he needed at least six months to decompress."
